utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-99-36-T, The Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brdjanin, good afternoon to you. Can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I can hear and understand the language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, Ann Sutherland, Julian Nicholls, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon to you all. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman. I'm here with David Cunningham and Aleksandar Vujic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good afternoon to you all. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Registrar. Yes, I received, and my colleagues received, earlier on today a copy of your motion, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we were asked if we could do it in writing, although we were intending to do this by way of oral application, which of course the Rules allow for, and I think Your Honour said a very long time ago that in the course of a trial oral applications would be quicker dealt with. But in order to give both Your Honours and Mr. Ackerman in writing the proposed application that the Prosecution will be making, that is why we drafted this motion at speed last night. It's very short, and I would wish to expand on certain aspects of it. I should say that I verbally informed Mr. Ackerman yesterday afternoon of what was going to be in this motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He didn't draft it for you, Ms. Korner, does he?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He didn't draft it for me, Your Honour, no, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, just on a very preliminary basis, what do you have to say about this motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: First of all, this is a matter of serious moment and absolutely should not be the subject of any kind of oral motion. It absolutely has to be a written motion because it's a matter which very likely, no matter how it comes out, would be part of the appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Forget that, because it's written now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Second of all, I've had it for less than two hours, I think. I think I received it around 12.15 today. Ordinarily I would have ten days to respond. I've had less than 10 minutes. That's just not fair. And I don't think it should be considered today at all. I think it would be totally unfair to consider it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The Court can shorten that ten days and give me a time to respond. Once I respond, then I think it can be talked about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. How much time do you want, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can do it by Monday. That's way less than ten days. That's what I'll do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's fair enough. You will do it by Monday. Okay. So is it okay, because we will need to again sit on Monday, if that is okay. If it's convenient for both of you. I would enjoin you to agree to that because Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday I am engaged in the Deronjic sentencing hearing. So I won't -- I can be available when I'm not sitting in Deronjic, but it would be top-heavy.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as -- as far as we're concerned, Your Honour, we have done this at sort of type of speed because Your Honour enjoined us if at all possible to call any rebuttal evidence if allowed to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- as soon as possible. As far as the Prosecution is concerned, we are content with any dates that Your Honour fixes. We are content to call this evidence, if allowed, at any time that Your Honours fix.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So as I say, in one sense we were merely trying to comply with Your Honours' request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. I think you know appreciate that, Ms. Korner, and I also, of course, appreciate that I cannot -- Mr. Ackerman insisted for his ten days, I think I would have crossed swords with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Should have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I think I can live with extending --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, when I did say Monday, I had in mind by the filing deadline of 4.00. Friday is going to be over when I get out of here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, you make it difficult for me. Please, try to understand my predicament. Next week, I have three days in which I am sitting in Deronjic. After that, I will be having in camera meetings with the other two Judges to come to a first conclusion because it's normal practice that we do that straight away after the sentencing hearing, which basically puts me in a situation where I am going to be really fully occupied this coming week with a lot of readings, hundreds of pages that I have to read between now and when we start and as we go along. Monday, I do not have a sitting. And if there is a courtroom available in the afternoon, we could sit in the afternoon. Otherwise, the only other day that I could think of is Friday of next week, but I don't know what to expect in the Deronjic sentencing hearing. So I mean, the idea now is to have the hearings spread over three days, three days. But it could -- we could go on on the fourth day without -- because there's evidence coming up, and there's a lot of things. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: My suggestion would be then that we do it as late as possible on Monday, maybe 3.00 or something like that. Or if that's not possible, then Friday. I really need some time, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's what's good for the goose is also good for the gander. I mean, the Prosecution must also be put in a position where if you raise legal matters, particularly in your response, they would have adequate notice, prior notice of it, so that if we have submissions, oral submissions -- I mean, I came prepared with case --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may it help if I make our position clear as to the -- what we say the law is. It may help Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, I object to this matter being raised today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are not going to argue it, Mr. Ackerman. I just want to hear what --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to assist, I hope Mr. Ackerman and Your Honours, to see what the position is as far as the Prosecution is concerned. This is purely subject to Mr. Ackerman's putting in a response to our motion with the law as he sees it. I am prepared to make certain concessions on the law which may assist Mr. Ackerman and may assist Your Honours. And that's why I think it might be helpful if I do that now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I suppose --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- rather than Mr. Ackerman making points which he doesn't need to because we'll concede them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think we can proceed along those lines at least for today. That would make your life easier, particularly when drawing up your response, Mr. Ackerman, from the legal point of view because what's going to be conceded need not be repeated. All right? Yes, go ahead, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: May I go into private session because I will have to touch on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Korner, if Mr. Ackerman files his motion, say, by noon or 1.00 on Monday, would you be prepared to argue the motion, say, at half past 3.00?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Is that fine with you, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, the big problem is whether we have a courtroom. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, while he's looking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We may have a courtroom already booked for Brdjanin throughout the entire...

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: While he's looking, the Prosecution had put some packets up on your Bench which I ask to be withdrawn. These are exhibits -- they are not there any more because Mr. Roberts has them now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know what you're talking about now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: They are the Laktasi exhibits that they want to use in rebuttal. I objected to those being given to you at this point and ask they be taken back off the Bench. Mr. Roberts now has them. And I respectfully request that you not look at them until I've had a chance to file my response because I believe there's a basis upon which I can argue that you should not even see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We definitely will not have a look. We will not even ask for them at least before we have read -- gone through your response and also heard the oral arguments on Monday, and then we decide.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect, Your Honours have as it were a two-fold role in cases like this. Your Honours have to make a decision on the basis of what is available to Your Honours. Your Honours cannot possibly make a decision as to the prejudice or otherwise or the importance of this evidence without seeing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But what I mean to say is that we will not bother ourselves with those documents before we have had Mr. Ackerman's response.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And at least have a clear purview of the legal points involved. Then obviously, there may become a point where they become very necessary. I see no point in reading them before I have read Mr. Ackerman's response.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we will liaise with Mr. Roberts as we go along. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next week, the date will be -- 26th is the first one, no? So this is Courtroom II. You have Milosevic there, you have Hadzihasanovic. Courtroom II, Courtroom III. Strugar, Blagojevic. We have a problem. We don't have a courtroom on Monday. We don't have a courtroom on Monday. Okay, I know Milosevic, yeah, I know what the problem is. Yeah. No, there is no way we can do anything there. The alternative, Mr. Ackerman and Ms. Korner, if it's okay with Judge Janu and Judge Taya and with both of you, we forget about Monday because if there is no courtroom, there is no courtroom, and we have the sitting on Wednesday, the 28th. I'm sitting in Deronjic in the afternoon. Courtroom III seems to be occupied in the morning. Courtroom II seems to be free. And Courtroom I seems to be occupied. So we only have the option of Wednesday morning in Courtroom II. Please check me out because this keeps getting updated. But this is today's. I mean, what I have in front of me is today's. See if she can place us anywhere on Monday afternoon, if she cannot then Wednesday morning, and it seems the only availability is Courtroom II at 9.00, from 9.00 to quarter to 2.00. Would that be suitable to either of you?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I'll come back to you -- it's okay with you, Judge Janu? - I'll come back to you later on when the registrar has contacted the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I then raise the next question of when Mr. Shoup is going to testify. We have been given today the full report, literally just now before Your Honours walked in. My preference would be, because of the shortness of time of getting the full report, to leave him on the 9th, but I understand that it's possible for him to come on the 2nd. And all that I want to know is we'll obviously comply with any ruling Your Honour makes of it on this, but which date will it be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, what's your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it makes no difference to me. He's ready to come. He can testify -- the 2nd I think is a holiday. He will have to testify on the 3rd or the 9th. And it's your choice, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, may I ask you. Because I would think that the sooner we get -- I frankly believe -- instead of believe, I frankly prefer to have the evidence in rebuttal, if that is granted, to be heard after Mr. Shoup has finished, to tell you the truth. And that means that I would appreciate if you could bring him forward. However, since the 2nd is a UN holiday, I don't want to deprive you of a day. You and/or Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm being given precisely seven days to, in breach of just about every rule going on expert evidence, to prepare for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But as I say, if Your Honours would prefer to have him called on the 3rd, then Your Honours -- then we will deal with that. All that we ask is how long are Your Honours going to give for examination-in-chief and cross?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know how much he requires in the first place. I think I recall you having said once about three days?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, my last estimate is two days, which is, I suppose, optimistic in view of a couple of things that have arisen. But there would be no problem with him staying over the weekend to the following Monday if we have to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's easy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He's prepared to be here. He's retired, so he's prepared to be here as long as it takes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And that gives us the opportunity --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: May I just say for the record, Your Honour, that I have absolutely no objection to Ms. Korner having additional time if the Court thinks that's appropriate. I'm just trying to accommodate the Court by bringing him earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And I agree with her, seven days is not a great deal of notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree. And if Ms. Korner needs more time -- are you bringing Mr. Donia here, Professor Donia here, by any chance while the Defence expert is giving evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We hadn't intended to, no, Your Honour. He can be here. But I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it would be -- because I have been thinking about this and discussing also with Judge Janu and Judge Taya. Professor Donia is your expert witness, not the Court's expert witness. And the expert witness that Mr. Ackerman is bringing forward is the Defence's expert witness, and this is precisely dealing with a matter which the three of us -- I mean, we certainly cannot claim to be experts ourselves on the matter. Now, in my jurisdiction, we usually resort to two, either of two alternatives. We either appoint our own expert, but at this point of the proceedings that may become not exactly very practical, might require us to wait further, and I would try to avoid that. We also use another alternative, and that is have the expert, the other expert of the opposite party present. And if necessary, if we have a point which we need clarification, if necessary even organise a confrontation between the two experts. That works. Believe me, it works. And it usually gives the trial judge and whoever is following the -- quite a broad view and idea of where to go. I mean, I've found it myself in my career extremely helpful. Of course, I cannot insist on -- I cannot insist on you... On the other hand, there is another point, Ms. Korner, that I would like to make clear. You know that under the Rules, we do have a right to put questions to witnesses. And we may need to put some further questions to Mr. Donia once the expert for the Defence has given evidence, especially if certain parts of Mr. Donia's expert evidence -- I mean, I don't know because I haven't read -- I haven't gone through your expert's report.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour is about to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It may present some problems for us if we just have two versions, one depicting the situation as white, the other one as black, and we get caught in the middle --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I don't know, because I haven't seen the report at all. I wasn't here, so I didn't even see the draft. Whether he specifically addresses any of the assertions made by Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Ackerman can tell us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If Mr. Ackerman can tell us. If he does, Your Honour, then we can, and Your Honours request, feel that it may be you want to put further questions to Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Maybe yes, maybe not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I agree. We can make arrangements to have Dr. Donia brought back to this Court. The summary that we got, I'm reminded, said that it was to rebut the evidence of Mr. Treanor as well and I'm not clear on what aspect. But Mr. Treanor, of course, is in the building, so there's no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But Mr. Donia isn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He's not. We would have to bring him from the United States.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I have some comments from you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What is it you'd like me to comment about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have obviously gone through the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose you are the only one, apart from your -- who has done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think Ms. Sutherland probably has read it, at least the initial draft, and maybe Mr. Nicholls has read it, at least the initial draft. So I'm not the only one. It's my -- I hesitate to commit myself in any significant way, but I think there's very little in there that involves a direct confrontation with the evidence of Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As I say --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He goes off on a really kind of different tack completely and deals with other matters, so I don't think there's much --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: -- "Dr. Donia says this and I disagree" in there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just -- let me see. This is -- how many pages long is it, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: 52 pages, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 52. So we can read it over the weekend. We can read it over the weekend, and -- Ms. Korner, if we think that Mr. Donia's presence here may be required, we will let you know, and of course we will inform Mr. Ackerman, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just simply say that the sooner the better because I know that he has many professional commitments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can imagine. Okay. The other thing, let's go into private session for a while while we are on this. It leads me to something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now. If you want to go back to private session, we can do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, let's go into private session again, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Hope is always the last -- hope is always the last to die, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Anything else, Mr. Ackerman? Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Janu? No. I thank you all. I thank you, Mr. Ackerman, for the expert's report. I look forward to your response on Monday, which should enable Judge Janu, Judge Taya and myself to be able to come to a decision in the course of next week, possibly not later than the end of next week. Thank you.
